simple_description: An excruciatingly severe, piercing headache strictly around or behind one eye, lasting 15 to 180 minutes, accompanied by eye redness, tearing, and a blocked nose on the same side, recurring in clusters.
medical_description: A severe strictly unilateral primary neurovascular headache classified among the trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias. Attacks last 15-180 minutes and occur from once every other day up to 8 times per day, accompanied by prominent ipsilateral cranial parasympathetic autonomic symptoms and physical restlessness or agitation.
affected_system: Hypothalamus (circadian pacemaker), trigeminovascular system, and cranial parasympathetic autonomic pathways (sphenopalatine ganglion).
symptoms: Excruciating, drilling, burning or piercing pain centered in or around one eye (orbital/supraorbital)
Strictly unilateral (always on the same side during a cluster period)
Ipsilateral eye tearing (lacrimation) and redness (conjunctival injection)
Ipsilateral nasal congestion or clear runny nose (rhinorrhea)
Eyelid drooping (ptosis) and pupil constriction (miosis) on the painful side
Marked physical restlessness, pacing the room or rocking (unlike migraine where patients lie still)
early_warning_signs: Mild discomfort, fullness, or shadowy ache around the eye starting 10-15 minutes prior
possible_causes: Hypothalamic activation triggering the trigeminal-autonomic reflex
Disruption of circadian biologic clock rhythmicity
risk_factors: Male sex (3 to 4 times more prevalent in men)
Heavy cigarette smoking and alcohol consumption (alcohol almost invariably triggers an attack during a cluster bout)
disease_types: Episodic cluster headache (bouts lasting 2 weeks to 3 months separated by remissions of >= 3 months)
Chronic cluster headache (attacks continuing for > 1 year without remission or with remissions < 3 months)
clinical_evaluation: Strict diagnostic criteria based on attack duration, frequency, autonomic features, and observed motor agitation. Physical exam during attack shows Horner-like signs.
diagnostic_tests: High-resolution 3T Brain MRI with pituitary and cavernous sinus protocol - Mandatory in all patients to exclude secondary structural lesions (pituitary adenoma, carotid dissection, cavernous sinus pathology)
treatment_overview: Dual strategy: Rapid abortive therapy with 100% high-flow normobaric oxygen or subcutaneous sumatriptan. Transitional bridging (oral corticosteroids or greater occipital nerve block) plus maintenance preventive therapy with Verapamil.
medication_classes: Acute abortive: 100% Normobaric Oxygen (12-15 L/min via non-rebreather mask for 15-20 min)
Subcutaneous Sumatriptan (6 mg) or Intranasal Zolmitriptan (5-10 mg)
Preventive first-line: Verapamil (high dose, monitored with serial ECG for PR interval)
Lithium carbonate, Topiramate, Galcanezumab (CGRP antibody approved for episodic cluster)
precautions: Strict abstinence from alcohol during active cluster periods
Avoid daytime naps which frequently provoke attacks
Do not give oral analgesics or opioids (they take 45+ minutes to absorb and are completely ineffective for cluster attacks)
prevention: Daily maintenance verapamil under cardiologist/neurologist supervision
Greater occipital nerve (GON) block with steroid and local anesthetic for rapid temporary suppression
complications: Severe psychological distress, depression, and high risk of suicide during bouts due to intolerable pain intensity
emergency_signs: First presentation of severe orbital pain without prior history (must rule out acute glaucoma or carotid artery dissection)
Sudden thunderclap onset or persistent Horner's syndrome outside of attacks

faqs.question: Why is pure oxygen used?
faqs.answer: Inhaling 100% oxygen at 12 to 15 liters per minute via a non-rebreather mask causes cerebral vasoconstriction and dampens trigeminal-parasympathetic activity, terminating an attack within 10 to 15 minutes without medication side effects.

faqs.question: Can regular painkillers help?
faqs.answer: No. Standard oral painkillers (like paracetamol or ibuprofen) are too slow to absorb and lack efficacy for the intense neuro-autonomic mechanisms of cluster headache.

hi.name: क्लस्टर सिरदर्द (Cluster headache)
hi.summary: एक आंख के पीछे होने वाला असहनीय, तेज जलन या ड्रिलिंग जैसा दर्द जिसके साथ उसी आंख से पानी, लाली और नाक बंद हो जाती है।
hi.advice: अटैक के समय 100% शुद्ध ऑक्सीजन मास्क द्वारा लेना सबसे असरदार उपाय है। तुरंत न्यूरोलॉजिस्ट से मिलें।

hinglish.name: Cluster Headache (Aankh ke peeche tez aag jaisa dard)
hinglish.summary: Ek aakh ke peeche aag jaisa dard hona jisme aakh laal ho jaye aur paani nikle, 15-180 minute tak rehta hai.
hinglish.advice: Normal painkiller kaam nahi karti. High-flow oxygen aur Verapamil therapy ke liye doctor se sampark karein.

ur.name: کلسٹر سر درد (آنکھ کے پیچھے شدید درد)
ur.summary: ایک آنکھ کے گرد انتہائی شدید درد جس کے ساتھ آنکھ کا سرخ ہونا، پانی آنا اور ناک بند ہونا شامل ہے۔
ur.advice: خالص آکسیجن کا استعمال اور نیورولوجسٹ کا مشورہ لازمی ہے۔
